testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A low air pressure warning signal:

options.text: Is not recommended on vehicles with air brakes.
Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
Is optional on vehicles with air brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
questions.explanation: All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal.

questions.question: Air brakes use ____ to function.
questions.correctAnswerText: Compressed air
questions.explanation: Air brakes use compressed air to work.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, what is the maximum safe leakage rate for a double combination vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: 3 psi in one minute.
questions.explanation: A double combination vehicle with air brakes should leak no more than 3 psi in one minute during a static leakage test. If it leaks faster, something needs to be repaired before driving.

questions.question: While driving downhill, you should brake until you reach a speed that is ____ below your safe speed, then release the brake pedal.
questions.correctAnswerText: 5 mph
questions.explanation: When driving downhill, brake until your speed is 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brake pedal. Repeat this process as needed.

questions.question: You should ____ if the low pressure warning signal activates while you are driving.

options.text: Stop where you are and park
Exit the roadway as soon as safely possible

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the roadway as soon as safely possible
questions.explanation: If the low pressure warning signal activates while driving, exit the roadway safely as soon as possible and park. Low air pressure means your brakes will not work well enough to stop safely.

questions.question: When using the controlled braking method in an emergency, you should:

options.text: Apply the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
Apply the brakes with about half of your usual force.
Apply the brakes so the wheels lock.
Apply the brakes with minimal pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: For controlled braking in an emergency, apply the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. Make small steering movements when braking this way.

questions.question: If air pressure drops to a level between ____, a visual low pressure warning signal should have already activated.
questions.correctAnswerText: 55 and 75 psi.
questions.explanation: The visual low pressure warning signal should activate before air pressure drops between 55 and 75 psi. This signal can be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: If your tractor has ABS but your trailer does not, the ABS:

options.text: Will still improve your steering control.
Will allow others to see when you brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will still improve your steering control.
questions.explanation: When the tractor has ABS but the trailer does not, the ABS will still improve steering control. Watch the trailer and ease off the brakes if it begins to swing out.

questions.question: What should happen before air pressure in an air brake system tank falls below 55 psi?

options.text: The vehicle will be unable to shift out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The warning light should activate.
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning signal must activate before air pressure drops below 55 psi. If the warning signal does not turn on during an inspection, the vehicle is not safe to drive.

questions.question: An air compressor governor stops the compressor from pumping air once the air tanks reach:
questions.correctAnswerText: 125 psi.
questions.explanation: An air compressor governor stops the compressor when air tanks reach 125 psi. This pressure level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: What can happen if you use parking brakes in very wet weather when temperatures are below freezing?

options.text: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
The brakes may suddenly release by themselves.
The brakes may become too smooth to work.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
questions.explanation: Do not use parking brakes in very wet weather when it is below freezing. The brakes could freeze in place, and you will not be able to move the vehicle.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, you should:

options.text: Pull out the air brake knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brake pedal down.
questions.explanation: To make a normal stop in a vehicle with air brakes, press the brake pedal down.

questions.question: What is commonly found in compressed air?
questions.correctAnswerText: Water
questions.explanation: Compressed air in air brake systems usually contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. Tanks must be drained regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: What do air storage tanks do?

options.text: Hold enough air for only one braking cycle.
Hold enough air for several braking cycles if the compressor stops working.
Hold air only during an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air for several braking cycles if the compressor stops working.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks store compressed air for braking. They hold enough air for you to brake several times even if the compressor stops working.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Cannot be used with air brakes.
Does not help in most driving situations.
Helps you stay in control when braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps you stay in control when braking.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) work with air brakes. ABS helps you stay in control by preventing the wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: What should you do with air tank drains?

options.text: Only use them when it is wet outside.
Use them to drain the tanks completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use them to drain the tanks completely.
questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and compressor oil from the air tanks. Always drain the tank completely.

questions.question: Where are foundation brakes used?

options.text: On each wheel of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On each wheel of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are used on each wheel. The most common type is the s-cam drum brake.

questions.question: What is true about an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: Cannot be used with air brakes.
Should only be used on dry pavement.
Helps you stay in control when braking.
Should only be used if all axles have ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps you stay in control when braking.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) work with air brakes. ABS helps you stay in control and stops the wheels from locking up during hard braking on slippery surfaces. ABS can help even if it is on only one axle.

questions.question: When using spring brakes with a heavy load, coming to a complete stop will:
questions.correctAnswerText: Take a long time.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes engage when air pressure is too low. A heavy vehicle will take a long time to stop using only spring brakes because they do not work on all axles.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, wait for the air compressor to build a minimum of ____ in both the primary and secondary systems.
questions.correctAnswerText: 100 psi
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, what happens after air pressure is lost and the spring brakes engage?

options.text: A separate air tank can release the spring brakes for a short time.
You can use the spring brakes to drive normally.
The air tanks refill automatically to a safe pressure level.

questions.correctAnswerText: A separate air tank can release the spring brakes for a short time.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with dual parking control valves have a separate air tank. This tank can temporarily release the spring brakes if they engage due to low air pressure. Pushing the correct control releases the spring brakes for a short time. This lets the driver move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: When you push the brake pedal, when do air brakes start to work?

options.text: Only when it is warm outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: After a short delay.
questions.explanation: Air takes time to travel through the air lines to reach the brakes. Air brakes do not work instantly. There is a brake lag of at least half a second between when you press the brake pedal and when the brakes actually start to work.

questions.question: What do air storage tanks do?

options.text: They are not allowed on vehicles.
They hold compressed air for the brakes.
They should be drained of excess air after every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: They hold compressed air for the brakes.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air used by the brake system. The number and size of these tanks varies by vehicle.

questions.question: When braking at 55 mph on dry pavement, how much extra distance does brake lag add to your stopping distance?
questions.correctAnswerText: 32 feet
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. When braking at 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to the total stopping distance.

questions.question: What makes up the emergency brake system?

options.text: Only parts of the parking brake system
Only parts of the service brake system
Parts of both the parking and service brake systems

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts of both the parking and service brake systems
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three separate braking systems: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.
